actual_scope: Add paid single-source scalar updates over GF(4) and determine the shortest dirty-connector path for the full 15-row, two-source coefficient family.
scope_change_reason: The card permits choosing one additional operation family on a small source count. I chose GF(4) scalar labels on single-source updates, rather than the already covered multi-source bundle families, and fixed the domain at two sources and all 15 nonzero coefficient rows.
bottleneck_link: For this exact interface batch, the shared scalar-source path reduces complete B-child invocations from 48 to 6 while preserving the 30 complete A readouts; the paid scalar multiplications and event descriptors are explicitly included. This is a recursive-interface cost result, not a selected-supplier or kappa claim.
stop_rule: Finish the exact two-source GF(4) pair-difference construction and lower bound; replay all length-one GF(4)-linear maps and dirty scalars for the 15 rows; verify the 48-to-6 source-child cost, event descriptor price, and failure controls. Do not search larger fields or source counts in this cycle.
evidence: CERTIFICATE.json gives a six-event closed path, six distinct prefixes, all 15 unique nonzero differences, the target boundary pairs and 36-event schedule. verify.py checks the k>=6 counting bound, exhausts 594 closed paths of lengths 1..5 (maximum coverage 7), replays 245760 dirty scalar cases, and checks omission/wrong-pair/readout controls. independent.py separately executes the literal stream on the same 245760 states. Complete cost comparison: 6 versus 48 B events; 4L versus 32L scalar XORs; 174 versus 342 descriptor bits under the stated prefix-record encoding. The predecessor baseline passed: PASS_UNIVERSAL_CONNECTOR_BOUNDARY pairings=945 max_coverage=31 queries=74 leaves=182. The full model also needs at least 30 target readouts by dirty-connector cancellation, so the 36 total root calls are optimal in the stated alphabet.
